answers.explanation: One bad cable only cuts off one device, but if the central device dies, everyone is cut off.
Each device has its own cable to the center, so only that one device loses its connection. That makes stars easy to troubleshoot.
Every device runs its own cable to a switch, or connects by Wi-Fi to an access point at the center.
Many paths between devices means no single link failure can cut anyone off.
All those redundant links need to be checked and agreed on, and some data may be sent more than one way.
Each device links to every other device: n − 1 = 7.
Stars connected to each other in a hierarchy make a tree. It's what large and spread-out networks usually look like.
The reading says the opposite: complex to configure, with increased cost. In return, they scale over long distances.
